method.label: Find the two types of hexagon angles

annotationRationale: Triangle angle sums calculate the two intersection angles, and vertical angles identify the second hexagon angle. Equilateral-triangle properties supply the 60-degree angles, while rotational symmetry accounts for all six vertices.
sourceMethod: Followed the official angle-chasing method using the 40-degree and 20-degree pairs of trisectors. Defined the intersections in words and explained which angles face the hexagon's interior.

review.mathCheck: The 40° rays give an intersection angle of 180° − 80° = 100°. The 20° rays give 140°, vertically opposite the corresponding hexagon angle. Both intersections lie within C's middle sector; 120° rotations give three vertices of each type. The minimum is 100°, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Problem 6, page 5. P corresponds to H and Q to E in the official figure; the candidate correctly explains the interior-angle orientations.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed angle-sum and vertical-angle nodes match the calculations. Equilateral properties and rotations appropriately support the construction and completeness argument. No material gap.
